1	<!-- What is established about the project (the language, the library, the tree and its tools, the specification and the plan) as it stands now, grouped by area: each entry the fact, its source and its test. One line per entry under its permanent number, `- F-87 **Title.** Text.`, written only with `explorations/coordinator/tools/record.py`. `FACTS-history.md` holds each change's provenance and the line as it stood before. What an entry holds and how it is written: the `coordinator` skill, `references/record.md`. -->
2	
3	# Facts on record
4	
5	## Execution model
6	
7	- F-7 **Walk and the compiled path share the parser and the phases, and only the compiled path runs the static type checker.** Walk switches the checker off, and no switch turns it on, so walk shows a type error only as a failed dispatch at run time. The phases and where the two paths part: the `fortress-repo` skill, "How a program runs". Detail: `repo-internals.md`, "The two worlds".
8	- F-9 **`fortress typecheck` checks a program against the compiler's library, `Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi`, so it is no oracle for walk programs.** `Shell.java` calls `useCompilerLibraries()` for the command (row 69). The checker reaches walk's programs after the switch-over (P-12).
9	- F-11 **The code generator boxes every number, and boxing is the main representational cost of microGPT-shaped array code.** So a compiled `RR64` loop holds no `dadd` or `dmul` (the `fortress-repo` skill, "The compiled run time"). In Java models of microGPT's three kernels, boxed elements cost 6.3× (dot product), 6.5× (matrix product) and 2.6× (row lift) over `double[]`. No such kernel compiles yet: the compiler prelude has no array type (row 305), and the arrays reach the compiled path with the one library (P-37). Detail: `perf-probes/kernels/REPORT.md` sections 2 and 4.
10	- F-12 **The compiled scalar `RR64` loop `bench1t` runs in 0.74 s, against 13.06 s without the fixes of rows 302 and 303, a pair timed in one session.** Two costs remain. The `for` becomes the compiler prelude's `countedseqloop`, a recursive split over boxed indices with a closure call per element. Each value is boxed (F-11). The 9.34 s of the boxing and kernels reports is the unfixed tree in another session, so compare only a pair timed in one session. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung0/REPORT.md`, "The four timings".
11	- F-17 **The bytecode cache can come up empty after a library order that reports exit 0.** Running the same commands again, one at a time, made the jars. The cause is not known. Check the five jars before a compiled run (the `fortress-repo` skill's `build-and-caches.md`, "The library order"). Detail: `perf-probes/boxing/REPORT.md` section 1.
12	- F-18 **Generic instantiations are stamped out at class-load time by ASM rewriting of template bytecode.** `InstantiatingClassloader` does it the first time a program uses an instance. A size is part of the stamped class's name, as in `pNatMeth$Box⟦3⟧`, and its descriptor inside the class is `RTTIsize.of("<n>")` (F-129). Detail: `perf-probes/nat/java.md` section 1.
13	- F-19 **Implicit parallelism: a `for` loop is parallel unless every generator is `seq`, and a tuple's elements and an operator's operands are evaluated in parallel.** `FORTRESS_THREADS` sizes the work-stealing pool (the `fortress-repo` skill, "Parallelism and mutable state"). No program under `explorations/` writes `spawn` or `also`. Source: `Specification/basic/expressions/tuple-expr.tex:23-24`, `operator-app.tex:59`.
14	- F-20 **Sizes, the `nat` and `int` static parameters, are values at run time and check shapes only.** The compiled checker checks them (F-67), and a sized program loads and runs compiled (F-129). No optimization uses them. Under walk, a `nat` parameter does not unify with an array built at run time, while a literal size does (row 23). Walk matches sizes at dispatch, and a mismatch is a `ProgramError`, "Failed to find any matching overload", that no `catch` takes (row 254). Source: `Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:97`.
15	- F-21 **The specification's own declaration of `Nothing` compiles on neither path, and the reason is name resolution, not code generation.** The Working Draft's `object Nothing extends Maybe[\T\] excludes Just[\T\] where {T extends Object}` stops at `excludes`: an object has no `excludes` clause. Without it, both paths report `T is undefined`: a `where` clause on an object binds no type variable of its `extends` clause, as row 17 holds for a trait. The specification marks it "Not allowed", and the library writes `Nothing[\T\]` (P-90). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-maybe/REPORT.md` section 5.
16	- F-22 **An exported function fails exactly as an exported variable does when a component's name differs from the api it exports, and the failure is the repository's, not codegen's.** Both paths look for an api's component under the api's own name, where the specification takes any component that exports it (row 320). `fortress link` and walk print "Could not find an implementation for API … on path", and a compiled run dies with `NoClassDefFoundError`. Name the api after its component. Gated by `compiler_tests/XXXExportVarRungXLinked.test`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-export-var/REPORT.md`.
17	- F-23 **A comment placed after a declaration that ends in an expression or a type becomes part of that declaration's source span and of the unambiguous name the parser derives from it.** The parser's `createSpan` trims back over spaces only, and a declaration that ends in `end` is unaffected (row 359). So a comment-only library edit can change the syntax tree, and a before-and-after comparison of parse trees or diagnostics maps positions back first. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-library-comments/REPORT.md` section 6, D1.
18	- F-24 **Under `walk`, a native can raise a Fortress exception that a Fortress `catch` sees.** It throws a `FortressError` that holds the exception's object, as `Int.overflow()` does for `IntegerOverflow` (F-132; row 347, fixed). Any other Java exception of a native becomes a `ProgramError`, which no `catch` takes, so a division by zero ends the run (row 336). Gated by the `overflows(...)` assertions of `tests/IntSemanticsRungI.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-int-semantics-walk/REPORT.md` section 4.1.
19	- F-25 **The compiled run's class loader takes its first load of a name under the JDK's class-loading lock, and a generic arm's first load is safe on four threads.** `InstantiatingClassloader.loadClass` locks `getClassLoadingLock(name)`, as the JDK's `ClassLoader` does (row 417, fixed). Gated by `compiler_tests/FirstLoadThreadsRungG`, which the gate's four-thread atomic runs also run. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-generic-runtime/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 12.
20	- F-26 **Walk chooses between a generic declaration and another on their declared domains, not by the order they are written in.** It builds P-45 under walk. A generic trait's functional method is still compared by its instances; a generic dotted method is compared on its declared domain where exactly one of the two declared domains lies inside the other (`MethodStaticArgDeclaredDomain`). A generic instance chosen by converting an argument dispatches again, except for overloaded methods. The symbolic instance reads the static parameters' kinds and bounds, not a `where` clause. Gated by `tests/DispatchDeclaredDomain.fss` and `DispatchConvertedAgain.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-dispatch/REPORT.md` section 5.1.
21	- F-27 **Walk's load check reads a generic declaration beside a plain one on declared domains, and covers an overlap through `comprises` clauses, where its parameter-by-parameter check refuses.** It builds P-46 and P-60 under walk. An overlap passes only if one declaration below both covers all of it. It reads two generic declarations on their declared domains too, by the same rules (F-252), and refuses one valid set (row 539). Gated by `tests/ComprisesMeetWalk.fss` and `GenericBesidePlain*.fss`, among others. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-dispatch/REPORT.md` sections 5.3 and 5.4.
22	- F-28 **Walk instantiates a generic declaration declared to return `Any`.** `MakeInferenceSpecific` treats `Any` as it treats a trait type (row 157, fixed). Its visitor has no case for 11 of the syntax tree's 18 concrete type classes, and of those only the dimension forms can be written as a return type. Gated by `tests/GenericReturningAny.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-dispatch/REPORT.md` section 3.
23	- F-29 **Walk checks at load the `comprises` clauses of the program's main component.** It refuses an extender of a closed trait that the clause does not allow. It does not yet read the library's clauses (rows 595, 596), another component's (row 551), an object expression's (row 597), or that a listed type extends each instantiation (row 598). A `.test` file beside a test of `tests/` names its expected refusal by `load_exception_contains`. Gated by `tests/Comprises*UnlistedExtender` and the `XXX` files of rows 487, 549, 551, 597 and 598. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-load-check/REPORT.md`.
24	## The checker and the one library
25	
26	- F-32 **The one library binds its natives by 424 `builtinPrimitive` calls, and the compiled path cannot reuse walk's glue classes behind them.** The glue classes take walk's boxed values. Against the compiler's static helpers, 147 bindings change only their text (P-58). 61 have a helper that nothing binds, 25 of them under a name that the compiler prelude gives another helper (row 348). 138 need a new helper, and 78 need more. Every program's output needs `Writer`'s natives. MicroGPT also needs `nanoTime`, whose compiled helper returns `RR64`, `getProgramArgsPrim`, which `System` calls as it loads, and `NativeArray`; the last two have no compiled analogue. They are PLAN's phase 4. Detail: `perf-probes/prelude/natives-shape.md` section 2.
27	- F-34 **Between the interpreter's library and bytecode stands the checker, not disambiguation, desugaring or code generation.** Compiled as it is, the library gives 1,417 disambiguation errors, all collisions between the two preludes, an artifact. With `FortressLibrary` the prelude, disambiguation, desugaring and the overload rewriting report none. Code generation, measured once, refuses 4 declarations that the checker passes: two `AsIfExpr`, one `LetFn` and one call on an intersection-typed receiver. The rest fall where the checker fails, or on synthesized overloads. The dispatch generator refuses 12 of 198 overload sets, each a functional method and a top-level function with one signature. Detail: `perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance-flat.md` sections 3 and 4.
28	- F-35 **The `FortressLibrary` api has 25 declarations with a dead size, a size parameter that occurs in no parameter type, return type or body.** They check clean (P-40). Where the component omits the dead size, the export checker reports the api's declaration missing. Six vector `DOT` and juxtaposition operators have this shape, `[\T, nat n, nat m, nat p\]` in the api and `[\T, nat n\]` in the component, and give one of the distance's export errors (F-53). P-40 lets the dead sizes go only by a diff shown to the curator with the switch-over's design. Detail: `perf-probes/nat/REPORT.md` sections 2 and 7.
29	- F-36 **The code generator's `FnNameInfo.boundsFor` gives a size parameter a size argument, and every other kind a type argument.** A `bool`, `dim`, `unit` or `opr` parameter still gets a type argument, a latent defect; the checker refuses the first three by name (F-67). A size symbol stays in the mangled name and needs no descriptor. Only a literal size reaches the class loader, which takes its descriptor from `RTTIsize.of` (F-129). Detail: `perf-probes/nat/java.md` sections 1 to 3.
30	- F-37 **The one library's own sizes are the literals 0 to 3, and a compiled `typecase` on a size tests the value's own class.** A `typecase` tells `Vec[\ZZ32,3\]` from `Vec[\ZZ32,4\]` compiled by one `INSTANCEOF`, also when the size is a static parameter. A `typecase` that is a whole function body, with clauses that need a coercion, fails in code generation, size or not (row 340). Gated by `compiler_tests/NatRtCase` and `NatRtCaseGen`. Detail: `reviews/size-runtime-design-brief.md` section 5; `perf-probes/nat/size-probes.md` section 4.
31	- F-38 **The compiled dispatcher chooses an overload arm generic in a size by the value's size, and the arm reads its size.** Called with an argument typed `Any`, the dispatcher reads the size off the value's descriptor. The checker's return-type rule compares the arms' own sizes (row 410). The dispatcher skips the bound `Object` that the compile path gives a size parameter (row 412). Gated by `compiler_tests/NatRtDisp`, `NatRtDispSize` and `NatRtDispTrait`. Detail: `perf-probes/nat/size-probes.md` section 2.
32	- F-39 **An operator static argument is a compile-time name on both paths and by the specification, and no code reads it at run time.** The specification and walk substitute its name into the trait's methods; the compiled path carries it in the class name, with no descriptor. Only two tests declare an `opr` static parameter. Compiled, `Op[\+\]()` dies with `NoSuchMethodError` on its descriptor's `factory()` (row 366). A three-line fix in `MethodInstantiater` works on its reproducer, and the row waits (P-123). Detail: `perf-probes/nat/opr-kind-history.md` sections 2 and 3.
33	- F-40 **A size costs a few kilobytes at load and nothing on the hot path, and only the overload dispatcher reads a size off a value.** No optimisation uses a size. A sized loop is no faster, since boxing and a transaction check per local variable cost about 31 ns per element. A call dispatched on a size costs about 4 to 20 ns more than a resolved one. The checker checks a shape once per call site; at run time, once per arm tried and per type test. Detail: `perf-probes/nat/size-cost.md`, "The answers".
34	- F-41 **The compiled dispatcher tests `DOT`'s shared size for equality in both directions before it chooses the shared-size arm.** It is the team's check for a type variable in two invariant positions. A mismatch goes to the catch-all on both paths, and the checker gives a static mismatch the catch-all's signature without an error. By reading, the matrix product's shared inner size takes the same check. A size made by `array[E](n)` gets one descriptor per number from `RTTIsize.of`. Gated by `compiler_tests/NatRtDot`. Detail: `perf-probes/nat/size-rung-probes.md` sections 2 and 3.
35	- F-42 **A unit's earlier error hides its overloading and return-type checks, and the checker refuses a local function's parameter left untyped.** `StaticChecker` runs the overloading rules only on a unit with no earlier error, so clearing an early error can raise a count (F-53). The checker refuses an untyped local function parameter, "Missing parameter type for i", as at top level (rows 620, 621). The specification leaves the inference there undescribed (Appendix I), so write the type. Detail: `perf-probes/nat/zero.md` section 1.
36	- F-43 **The overloading checker's memo hides errors by build order, so every count runs with it off.** The switch is `fortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false`, which the gate's stages set. F-226 gives how the checker renames an inherited method's static parameters. Detail: `perf-probes/nat/triage.md` section 1.
37	- F-44 **The compiled checker enforces the designers' "multiple instantiation exclusion" and relies on it, and the one library meets it.** The return-type rule relies on it, so relaxed alone it admits programs that die with `IncompatibleClassChangeError`. Walk lacks it (row 416). P-43 keeps it. The library meets it through `TotalComparison`'s supertypes (row 461), `AnyMaybe` extending `AnyUniqueItem` alone, and `andCondCombine` choosing `andRelCond`, so a program's own `ANDCOND` of two relational predicates is not relational under walk (row 458). Detail: `reviews/multiple-instantiation-exclusion.md` sections 1, 2 and 5.
38	- F-45 **Without the exclusion rule, every dispatcher must call its generic arms at its own static arguments, and no published work resolves double membership under run-time dispatch.** These prices decided P-43. F-136 builds that call for template dispatchers; generic dotted methods, other dispatchers, and `opr` and `nat` arguments lack it (rows 495, 496). The 2012 patents' forest rule lets a self-typed generic stand at several instantiations along a chain, but alone it leaves the specialisation hole open; F-46 closes it. Detail: `reviews/mie-probes/scope-call-site-dispatch.md` section 3; `literature.md` beside it.
39	- F-46 **Route C, the patents' forest rule with a return-type rule over every level of a chain, closes the specialisation hole, but a return to it needs work beyond the checker.** Built as a shadow, it refuses 25 pairs of the nested tower's declarations. Completing the tower needs `comprises T` on the eight self-typed traits, which overflows the checker. Leaving P-43 for it needs the tower un-flattened, the call-site fix in every dispatcher, a method per level in the code generator, walk's work and a way past the overflow. Detail: `reviews/mie-probes/route-c-experiment.md` sections 2 to 4.
40	- F-47 **The exclusion rule refuses some of the specification's own examples, and a parametric object with a factory, or a widening function, runs in their place on both paths.** F-167 lists them. The where-clause examples stop earlier on both paths, at `T is undefined`. A marker object with a coercion in the generic trait also runs compiled, and walk applies such a coercion (row 389). The 2012 `covariant` keyword passes the checker and dies at run time (row 404), and a generic coercion is refused as a cyclic hierarchy. Route C (F-46) would rescue none of these examples. Detail: `reviews/spec-refused-examples.md`, "What was found".
41	- F-48 **The compiled checker's exclusion rule compares type arguments and literal sizes only, and its abstract-method check does not substitute an operator argument.** Two booleans, or a static parameter against another argument, count as no exclusion (rows 406, 414). Compiled, a subtrait that inherits an abstract method named by an operator static argument is refused even at one instantiation; the specification and walk substitute the name. <!-- What is established about the project (the language, the library, the tree and its tools, the specification and the plan) as it stands now, grouped by area: each entry the fact, its source and its test. One line per entry under its permanent number, `- F-87 **Title.** Text.`, written only with `explorations/coordinator/tools/record.py`. `FACTS-history.md` holds each change's provenance and the line as it stood before. What an entry holds and how it is written: the `coordinator` skill, `references/record.md`. -->

# Facts on record

## Execution model

- F-7 **Walk and the compiled path share the parser and the phases, and only the compiled path runs the static type checker.** Walk switches the checker off, and no switch turns it on, so walk shows a type error only as a failed dispatch at run time. The phases and where the two paths part: the `fortress-repo` skill, "How a program runs". Detail: `repo-internals.md`, "The two worlds".
- F-9 **`fortress typecheck` checks a program against the compiler's library, `Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi`, so it is no oracle for walk programs.** `Shell.java` calls `useCompilerLibraries()` for the command (row 69). The checker reaches walk's programs after the switch-over (P-12).
- F-11 **The code generator boxes every number, and boxing is the main representational cost of microGPT-shaped array code.** So a compiled `RR64` loop holds no `dadd` or `dmul` (the `fortress-repo` skill, "The compiled run time"). In Java models of microGPT's three kernels, boxed elements cost 6.3× (dot product), 6.5× (matrix product) and 2.6× (row lift) over `double[]`. No such kernel compiles yet: the compiler prelude has no array type (row 305), and the arrays reach the compiled path with the one library (P-37). Detail: `perf-probes/kernels/REPORT.md` sections 2 and 4.
- F-12 **The compiled scalar `RR64` loop `bench1t` runs in 0.74 s, against 13.06 s without the fixes of rows 302 and 303, a pair timed in one session.** Two costs remain. The `for` becomes the compiler prelude's `countedseqloop`, a recursive split over boxed indices with a closure call per element. Each value is boxed (F-11). The 9.34 s of the boxing and kernels reports is the unfixed tree in another session, so compare only a pair timed in one session. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung0/REPORT.md`, "The four timings".
- F-17 **The bytecode cache can come up empty after a library order that reports exit 0.** Running the same commands again, one at a time, made the jars. The cause is not known. Check the five jars before a compiled run (the `fortress-repo` skill's `build-and-caches.md`, "The library order"). Detail: `perf-probes/boxing/REPORT.md` section 1.
- F-18 **Generic instantiations are stamped out at class-load time by ASM rewriting of template bytecode.** `InstantiatingClassloader` does it the first time a program uses an instance. A size is part of the stamped class's name, as in `pNatMeth$Box⟦3⟧`, and its descriptor inside the class is `RTTIsize.of("<n>")` (F-129). Detail: `perf-probes/nat/java.md` section 1.
- F-19 **Implicit parallelism: a `for` loop is parallel unless every generator is `seq`, and a tuple's elements and an operator's operands are evaluated in parallel.** `FORTRESS_THREADS` sizes the work-stealing pool (the `fortress-repo` skill, "Parallelism and mutable state"). No program under `explorations/` writes `spawn` or `also`. Source: `Specification/basic/expressions/tuple-expr.tex:23-24`, `operator-app.tex:59`.
- F-20 **Sizes, the `nat` and `int` static parameters, are values at run time and check shapes only.** The compiled checker checks them (F-67), and a sized program loads and runs compiled (F-129). No optimization uses them. Under walk, a `nat` parameter does not unify with an array built at run time, while a literal size does (row 23). Walk matches sizes at dispatch, and a mismatch is a `ProgramError`, "Failed to find any matching overload", that no `catch` takes (row 254). Source: `Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:97`.
- F-21 **The specification's own declaration of `Nothing` compiles on neither path, and the reason is name resolution, not code generation.** The Working Draft's `object Nothing extends Maybe[\T\] excludes Just[\T\] where {T extends Object}` stops at `excludes`: an object has no `excludes` clause. Without it, both paths report `T is undefined`: a `where` clause on an object binds no type variable of its `extends` clause, as row 17 holds for a trait. The specification marks it "Not allowed", and the library writes `Nothing[\T\]` (P-90). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-maybe/REPORT.md` section 5.
- F-22 **An exported function fails exactly as an exported variable does when a component's name differs from the api it exports, and the failure is the repository's, not codegen's.** Both paths look for an api's component under the api's own name, where the specification takes any component that exports it (row 320). `fortress link` and walk print "Could not find an implementation for API … on path", and a compiled run dies with `NoClassDefFoundError`. Name the api after its component. Gated by `compiler_tests/XXXExportVarRungXLinked.test`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-export-var/REPORT.md`.
- F-23 **A comment placed after a declaration that ends in an expression or a type becomes part of that declaration's source span and of the unambiguous name the parser derives from it.** The parser's `createSpan` trims back over spaces only, and a declaration that ends in `end` is unaffected (row 359). So a comment-only library edit can change the syntax tree, and a before-and-after comparison of parse trees or diagnostics maps positions back first. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-library-comments/REPORT.md` section 6, D1.
- F-24 **Under `walk`, a native can raise a Fortress exception that a Fortress `catch` sees.** It throws a `FortressError` that holds the exception's object, as `Int.overflow()` does for `IntegerOverflow` (F-132; row 347, fixed). Any other Java exception of a native becomes a `ProgramError`, which no `catch` takes, so a division by zero ends the run (row 336). Gated by the `overflows(...)` assertions of `tests/IntSemanticsRungI.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-int-semantics-walk/REPORT.md` section 4.1.
- F-25 **The compiled run's class loader takes its first load of a name under the JDK's class-loading lock, and a generic arm's first load is safe on four threads.** `InstantiatingClassloader.loadClass` locks `getClassLoadingLock(name)`, as the JDK's `ClassLoader` does (row 417, fixed). Gated by `compiler_tests/FirstLoadThreadsRungG`, which the gate's four-thread atomic runs also run. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-generic-runtime/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 12.
- F-26 **Walk chooses between a generic declaration and another on their declared domains, not by the order they are written in.** It builds P-45 under walk. A generic trait's functional method is still compared by its instances; a generic dotted method is compared on its declared domain where exactly one of the two declared domains lies inside the other (`MethodStaticArgDeclaredDomain`). A generic instance chosen by converting an argument dispatches again, except for overloaded methods. The symbolic instance reads the static parameters' kinds and bounds, not a `where` clause. Gated by `tests/DispatchDeclaredDomain.fss` and `DispatchConvertedAgain.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-dispatch/REPORT.md` section 5.1.
- F-27 **Walk's load check reads a generic declaration beside a plain one on declared domains, and covers an overlap through `comprises` clauses, where its parameter-by-parameter check refuses.** It builds P-46 and P-60 under walk. An overlap passes only if one declaration below both covers all of it. It reads two generic declarations on their declared domains too, by the same rules (F-252), and refuses one valid set (row 539). Gated by `tests/ComprisesMeetWalk.fss` and `GenericBesidePlain*.fss`, among others. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-dispatch/REPORT.md` sections 5.3 and 5.4.
- F-28 **Walk instantiates a generic declaration declared to return `Any`.** `MakeInferenceSpecific` treats `Any` as it treats a trait type (row 157, fixed). Its visitor has no case for 11 of the syntax tree's 18 concrete type classes, and of those only the dimension forms can be written as a return type. Gated by `tests/GenericReturningAny.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-dispatch/REPORT.md` section 3.
- F-29 **Walk checks at load the `comprises` clauses of the program's main component.** It refuses an extender of a closed trait that the clause does not allow. It does not yet read the library's clauses (rows 595, 596), another component's (row 551), an object expression's (row 597), or that a listed type extends each instantiation (row 598). A `.test` file beside a test of `tests/` names its expected refusal by `load_exception_contains`. Gated by `tests/Comprises*UnlistedExtender` and the `XXX` files of rows 487, 549, 551, 597 and 598. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-load-check/REPORT.md`.
## The checker and the one library

- F-32 **The one library binds its natives by 424 `builtinPrimitive` calls, and the compiled path cannot reuse walk's glue classes behind them.** The glue classes take walk's boxed values. Against the compiler's static helpers, 147 bindings change only their text (P-58). 61 have a helper that nothing binds, 25 of them under a name that the compiler prelude gives another helper (row 348). 138 need a new helper, and 78 need more. Every program's output needs `Writer`'s natives. MicroGPT also needs `nanoTime`, whose compiled helper returns `RR64`, `getProgramArgsPrim`, which `System` calls as it loads, and `NativeArray`; the last two have no compiled analogue. They are PLAN's phase 4. Detail: `perf-probes/prelude/natives-shape.md` section 2.
- F-34 **Between the interpreter's library and bytecode stands the checker, not disambiguation, desugaring or code generation.** Compiled as it is, the library gives 1,417 disambiguation errors, all collisions between the two preludes, an artifact. With `FortressLibrary` the prelude, disambiguation, desugaring and the overload rewriting report none. Code generation, measured once, refuses 4 declarations that the checker passes: two `AsIfExpr`, one `LetFn` and one call on an intersection-typed receiver. The rest fall where the checker fails, or on synthesized overloads. The dispatch generator refuses 12 of 198 overload sets, each a functional method and a top-level function with one signature. Detail: `perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance-flat.md` sections 3 and 4.
- F-35 **The `FortressLibrary` api has 25 declarations with a dead size, a size parameter that occurs in no parameter type, return type or body.** They check clean (P-40). Where the component omits the dead size, the export checker reports the api's declaration missing. A helper that raises a Fortress exception names a compiled-prelude class, which walk ends as a `FortressImplementationError`. A helper over compiled-world types cannot take walk's values. Detail: `perf-probes/prelude/natives-shape.md` section 1.

A trait's or object's `throws` clause and contract never reach it, since the disambiguator drops them (row 781). The `fortress-repo` skill's `references/compiler.md`, "What the compiled path cannot compile yet", gives this refusal and the constructs that the code generator has no case for, a local function among them (row 304). 1	<!-- The curator's decisions about the project (the language, the library, the tree and its tools, the specification and the plan) as they stand now. One line per entry under its permanent number, `- P-48 **Title.** Text.`, written only with `explorations/coordinator/tools/record.py`. `POSITIONS-history.md` holds each change's provenance and the line as it stood before. What an entry holds and how it is written: the `coordinator` skill, `references/record.md`. How the curator and the coordinator work is that skill's, and what is established is in `FACTS.md`; neither is repeated here. -->
2	
3	# Pavol's positions, decisions and known ground
4	
5	## The goal
6	
7	- P-7 **The goal is to finish what the designers intended, measured by one program, microGPT, compiled to bytecode and running fast.** The judge is `Specification/`, the Working Draft of February 2011 as the revival revises it, with the 2012 Types chapter cited beside it (P-25). The language is not redesigned. The specification is a living document that states the revival's changes (P-95). The floor to measure against is a pure-Java microGPT, not yet written (PLAN phase 6).
8	- P-8 **Where the designers left no word, he decides by the goal, a compiled microGPT running fast, not by type-theoretic purity, and stays true to the spirit of Fortress.** He accepts the language's unfinished corners rather than stall in theory. He has not read the specification, the type papers or the library, and takes the designers to have known more than he does. So a review checks his decisions against their intent, for errors of commission and of omission; its items are decisions in this file. Detail: `reviews/decisions-review/judgement.md`, "In short".
9	- P-9 **The search is for microGPT's most readable expression.** In his words, "we are searching for the optimal expression of the microGPT algorithm for readability." The two sources are Fortress's mathematical notation and Iverson's APL notation, with Hsu's data design for data-flow algorithms. The flat program in Hsu's style, C4, fell short, so polishing happens in the vocabulary, the operations the model is written in. C4 is the APL program's target form. Its hyperparameters are tuple bindings, the form an APL strand assignment expands to; the semicolon form of those lines is set aside.
10	- P-10 **The APL side quest is closed: its remaining ground, tacit functions, characters and nested arrays, is not pursued.** Its sub-language expands APL to Fortress code over native arrays, and its APL microGPT program stays in the walk check (P-30).
11	- P-11 **The 2D notation is a gimmick: no work on it unless he asks.** Fortify's mathematical rendering bakes one view of a computation into the syntax, though the same mathematics can be written many ways. APL's one glyph for each transformation does that better. It is presentation only, off the path, and no argument for Fortress.
12	- P-12 **The type checker on interpreter programs comes after the switch-over.** He wants the checker usable on the programs that walk runs, and sees it as low-hanging fruit. Today it checks only against the compiler's prelude (F-9). It comes once walk also takes the static coercions that the checker inserts (P-59).
13	
14	## History he knows (do not re-explain)
15	
16	- P-16 **He reads the project's end as the price of doing no work on performance.** DARPA's HPCS did not take Sun into its third phase in 2006, and the project went on at Sun Labs until 2012. The team worked on syntax, and the compiler that was to make the mathematical types fast never came; the funding was cut for good reason.
17	- P-17 **Unboxed doubles and arrays of doubles are required: without them the revival misses its point.** The code generator boxes every number, and boxing is the main cost on microGPT's array kernels (F-11). Boxing is measured on microGPT-shaped kernels, not on a scalar loop with literals and a `:=` accumulator, which microGPT never runs. The storage is P-84's decision; unboxed arithmetic is PLAN phase 6 (P-33).
18	- P-18 **He is coming round to Hsu's view that language paradigms are accidental complexity.**
19	- P-19 **The tree is not described as the third-party port's migration grafted on its history.** The files that still say so wait for the lineage cleanup (PLAN, "Off the path, parked"), which `coordinator/lineage.md`, "Files that still repeat it", lists. His plan to make the graft-free `clean-ladder` branch `main` is not carried out (F-165).
20	
21	## Decisions on record
22	
23	### The standard and the sources
24	
25	- P-25 **The specification stays the standard, the Types chapter beside it.** Where the Types chapter of the team's unfinished 2012 restart (F-166) covers a topic, it is cited beside `Specification/` as the designers' later word. On the rules that the revival revises, it is their latest intent, which the goal is to finish. It covers the exclusion rule, as instantiation exclusion in its two-part form, the `covariant` modifier, and `Bottom`, which no program can write.
26	- P-26 **The type group's late positions outweigh the specification's early text where they conflict.** The early text was a wish. The type group then made the language run, for performance and with specialization a must, and learned what is feasible. So their later word wins: the exclusion rule, specialization kept, the compiler prelude's tower flattened in 2009 and 2010 (P-43), Naden's 2012 write-up, the POPL 2019 paper. The implementers' later word also outweighs unfinished text. The revival does not second-guess them: it knows less than they did.
27	- P-27 **The library's own practice is the standard.** What microGPT invented goes into the standard library, in the library's own style. Whoever extends the library first studies how it does the same kind of thing, and follows that pattern; exclusion, for one, is all over it. He had to find the diagonal's override himself (P-88) because that study was skipped. No fix is designed from the specification alone or from a workaround on the user's side.
28	- P-28 **Fleshing out the standard library is a very important task.** Next is the algebraic layer: `Ring`, `Field` and what the matrices and tensors of machine learning need, so that the library's traits reach them. It goes into the standard library itself (P-27), not into a tree of the revival's own.
29	- P-29 **Walk's speed is irrelevant to every judgement of Fortress's performance.** Walk is hundreds of times slower than Python's interpreter. So no performance decision of any kind, and no edit of C4, the flat model program, for speed, until microGPT runs compiled. The gate never runs the two microGPT programs, too long-running to be tests: it compiles them and records the phase that each reaches. A run of them, once possible, goes to a stage that does not gate.
30	- P-30 **The microGPT walk check after a batch runs in under a minute.** It runs about two forward-and-backward passes against the reference values, which shows that the model's mathematics still works and that the library's changes did not break it. The full check programs run only when asked. A slower check is to him a waste of time.
31	- P-32 **The territory map (`coordinator/map/`) maps the tree down to where the design intent is written, in the papers as well as the specification.** It exists so that nothing on record is found again from scratch.
32	- P-33 **The plan (`coordinator/PLAN.md`) has six phases, approved with their workers.** Phases 1 and 2 are landed: the wrapping operators, the revised specification, the run-time sizes, the flat number tower and the overflow natives. 3 is the checker at a true zero; 4, the switch-over, natives then names; 5, microGPT compiles: its static types, the array design and the code generator's holes; 6, microGPT fast. Where the work stands: PLAN's "Where we stand". Re-approval row 41 (ledger row 320: a component named apart from its api does not link) joins the switch-over's design.
33	
34	### The one library and the compiled checker
35	
36	- P-37 **One library, the interpreter's, is the library the compiler checks.** The interpreter's `FortressLibrary` and `FortressBuiltin` become the compiled path's library. He sees the compiler's prelude (`CompilerLibrary`, `CompilerBuiltin`, `CompilerAlgebra`) as a bootstrap to remove, so no declaration goes into it, and its three files are deleted at the switch-over with their tests kept. Code-generator rungs go on. How the checker comes to accept the library is a plan shown to him step by step, not a question to ask again. Still to build: PLAN phase 4.
37	- P-38 **The compiler prelude's defects are not repaired: they go with it at the switch-over.** Its `Maybe` block and its `REM` guard `if other = -1 then 0` stay as landed until the prelude is deleted, and their tests stay. Then the compiled tests respell its reversed wrapping and saturating operators (row 348), `ZZ64`'s compiled shift closes (row 381), and the specification's `shift` reaches the compiled path (row 383). `XXXShiftDeclRungI` is then promoted, and the switch-over batch finds the compiler tests that bind `shift`, a reserved name from then on. Still to build: PLAN phase 4.
38	- P-39 **The checker count is measured in every gate and never turns the gate red.** The gate reports the count stage on its own. The distance to the switch-over (F-53), over all apis and components, is a report-only stage of the phase-3 gates, whose work drives it down.

111	- P-150 **No resident compiler is built.** One warm JVM that serves many Fortress commands, as Scala 2's `fsc` did, would save at most 1.8 % of the workers' time, so the speed work goes to the checker itself (P-148). It is weighed again only if that share grows much, for example once programs are compiled often after the switch-over.

<!-- The curator's decisions about the project (the language, the library, the tree and its tools, the specification and the plan) as they stand now. One line per entry under its permanent number, `- P-48 **Title.** Text.`, written only with `explorations/coordinator/tools/record.py`. `POSITIONS-history.md` holds each change's provenance and the line as it stood before. What an entry holds and how it is written: the `coordinator` skill, `references/record.md`. How the curator and the coordinator work is that skill's, and what is established is in `FACTS.md`; neither is repeated here. -->

# Pavol's positions, decisions and known ground

## The goal

- P-7 **The goal is to finish what the designers intended, measured by one program, microGPT, compiled to bytecode and running fast.** The judge is `Specification/`, the Working Draft of February 2011 as the revival revises it, with the 2012 Types chapter cited beside it (P-25). The language is not redesigned. The specification is a living document that states the revival's changes (P-95). The floor to measure against is a pure-Java microGPT, not yet written (PLAN phase 6).
- P-8 **Where the designers left no word, he decides by the goal, a compiled microGPT running fast, not by type-theoretic purity, and stays true to the spirit of Fortress.** He accepts the language's unfinished corners rather than stall in theory. He has not read the specification, the type papers or the library, and takes the designers to have known more than he does. So a review checks his decisions against their intent, for errors of commission and of omission; its items are decisions in this file. Detail: `reviews/decisions-review/judgement.md`, "In short".
- P-9 **The search is for microGPT's most readable expression.** In his words, "we are searching for the optimal expression of the microGPT algorithm for readability." The two sources are Fortress's mathematical notation and Iverson's APL notation, with Hsu's data design for data-flow algorithms. The flat program in Hsu's style, C4, fell short, so polishing happens in the vocabulary, the operations the model is written in. C4 is the APL program's target form. Its hyperparameters are tuple bindings, the form an APL strand assignment expands to; the semicolon form of those lines is set aside.
- P-10 **The APL side quest is closed: its remaining ground, tacit functions, characters and nested arrays, is not pursued.** Its sub-language expands APL to Fortress code over native arrays, and its APL microGPT program stays in the walk check (P-30).
- P-11 **The 2D notation is a gimmick: no work on it unless he asks.** Fortify's mathematical rendering bakes one view of a computation into the syntax, though the same mathematics can be written many ways. APL's one glyph for each transformation does that better. It is presentation only, off the path, and no argument for Fortress.
- P-12 **The type checker on interpreter programs comes after the switch-over.** He wants the checker usable on the programs that walk runs, and sees it as low-hanging fruit. Today it checks only against the compiler's prelude (F-9). It comes once walk also takes the static coercions that the checker inserts (P-59).

## History he knows (do not re-explain)

- P-16 **He reads the project's end as the price of doing no work on performance.** DARPA's HPCS did not take Sun into its third phase in 2006, and the project went on at Sun Labs until 2012. The team worked on syntax, and the compiler that was to make the mathematical types fast never came; the funding was cut for good reason.
- P-17 **Unboxed doubles and arrays of doubles are required: without them the revival misses its point.** The code generator boxes every number, and boxing is the main cost on microGPT's array kernels (F-11). Boxing is measured on microGPT-shaped kernels, not on a scalar loop with literals and a `:=` accumulator, which microGPT never runs. The storage is P-84's decision; unboxed arithmetic is PLAN phase 6 (P-33).
- P-18 **He is coming round to Hsu's view that language paradigms are accidental complexity.**
- P-19 **The tree is not described as the third-party port's migration grafted on its history.** The files that still say so wait for the lineage cleanup (PLAN, "Off the path, parked"), which `coordinator/lineage.md`, "Files that still repeat it", lists. His plan to make the graft-free `clean-ladder` branch `main` is not carried out (F-165).

## Decisions on record

### The standard and the sources

- P-25 **The specification stays the standard, the Types chapter beside it.** Where the Types chapter of the team's unfinished 2012 restart (F-166) covers a topic, it is cited beside `Specification/` as the designers' later word. On the rules that the revival revises, it is their latest intent, which the goal is to finish. It covers the exclusion rule, as instantiation exclusion in its two-part form, the `covariant` modifier, and `Bottom`, which no program can write.
- P-26 **The type group's late positions outweigh the specification's early text where they conflict.** The early text was a wish. The type group then made the language run, for performance and with specialization a must, and learned what is feasible. So their later word wins: the exclusion rule, specialization kept, the compiler prelude's tower flattened in 2009 and 2010 (P-43), Naden's 2012 write-up, the POPL 2019 paper. The implementers' later word also outweighs unfinished text. The revival does not second-guess them: it knows less than they did.
- P-27 **The library's own practice is the standard.** What microGPT invented goes into the standard library, in the library's own style. Whoever extends the library first studies how it does the same kind of thing, and follows that pattern; exclusion, for one, is all over it. He had to find the diagonal's override himself (P-88) because that study was skipped. No fix is designed from the specification alone or from a workaround on the user's side.
- P-28 **Fleshing out the standard library is a very important task.** Next is the algebraic layer: `Ring`, `Field` and what the matrices and tensors of machine learning need, so that the library's traits reach them. It goes into the standard library itself (P-27), not into a tree of the revival's own.
- P-29 **Walk's speed is irrelevant to every judgement of Fortress's performance.** Walk is hundreds of times slower than Python's interpreter. So no performance decision of any kind, and no edit of C4, the flat model program, for speed, until microGPT runs compiled. The gate never runs the two microGPT programs, too long-running to be tests: it compiles them and records the phase that each reaches. A run of them, once possible, goes to a stage that does not gate.
- P-30 **The microGPT walk check after a batch runs in under a minute.** It runs about two forward-and-backward passes against the reference values, which shows that the model's mathematics still works and that the library's changes did not break it. The full check programs run only when asked. A slower check is to him a waste of time.
- P-32 **The territory map (`coordinator/map/`) maps the tree down to where the design intent is written, in the papers as well as the specification.** It exists so that nothing on record is found again from scratch.
- P-33 **The plan (`coordinator/PLAN.md`) has six phases, approved with their workers.** Phases 1 and 2 are landed: the wrapping operators, the revised specification, the run-time sizes, the flat number tower and the overflow natives. 3 is the checker at a true zero; 4, the switch-over, natives then names; 5, microGPT compiles: its static types, the array design and the code generator's holes; 6, microGPT fast. Where the work stands: PLAN's "Where we stand". Re-approval row 41 (ledger row 320: a component named apart from its api does not link) joins the switch-over's design.

### The one library and the compiled checker

- P-37 **One library, the interpreter's, is the library the compiler checks.** The interpreter's `FortressLibrary` and `FortressBuiltin` become the compiled path's library. He sees the compiler's prelude (`CompilerLibrary`, `CompilerBuiltin`, `CompilerAlgebra`) as a bootstrap to remove, so no declaration goes into it, and its three files are deleted at the switch-over with their tests kept. Code-generator rungs go on. How the checker comes to accept the library is a plan shown to him step by step, not a question to ask again. Still to build: PLAN phase 4.
- P-38 **The compiler prelude's defects are not repaired: they go with it at the switch-over.** Its `Maybe` block and its `REM` guard `if other = -1 then 0` stay as landed until the prelude is deleted, and their tests stay. Then the compiled tests respell its reversed wrapping and saturating operators (row 348), `ZZ64`'s compiled shift closes (row 381), and the specification's `shift` reaches the compiled path (row 383). `XXXShiftDeclRungI` is then promoted, and the switch-over batch finds the compiler tests that bind `shift`, a reserved name from then on. Still to build: PLAN phase 4.
- P-39 **The checker count is measured in every gate and never turns the gate red.** The gate reports the count stage on its own. The distance to the switch-over (F-53), over all apis and components, is a report-only stage of the phase-3 gates, whose work drives it down.
- P-40 **Sizes are checked, and a size left unknown is an error only where it is used.** The checker checks `nat` and `int` static parameters and refuses a size beyond `NN32` or `ZZ32` (F-140). Storage refuses a JVM array length over 2^31-1. A size that inference leaves unknown is an error only when it reaches a type, a name or a value. How the checker represents it is not his choice. A size that a call cannot fix refuses the call, also inside an overload set, instead of dropping the arm (row 400, its compiled half open). Every static argument but an operator counts in the exclusion rule; booleans join once the checker has boolean parameters (row 406). A size used as a value converts to `ZZ32` as a numeral does (row 485). The api's 25 unused sizes (F-35) go only by a diff shown to him with the switch-over's design.
- P-41 **At run time a size travels as the descriptor that a type argument has (design B).** It fills the slot that the team's code generator reserved. Each number has one descriptor, from a table, with no holder class, as the team instantiates types. Operator static arguments stay compile-time names (F-39): he sees no need to unify them.
- P-42 **An unbounded type parameter's implicit bound is `Any`, not `Object`.** `Any` holds tuples, functions and `()`, which `Object` does not, and the library instantiates its generic containers at tuples, arrays indexed by pairs among them. The specification states the bound, with a callout that keeps the Working Draft's `Object`. The compile path's `Object` bound departs from it until the switch-over (row 412).
- P-43 **The exclusion rule stays, and the number tower is flat (route A).** The compiled checker keeps the multiple instantiation exclusion rule. So the library's numbers are flat, as the team (Chase, Ryu, Maessen and Allen) flattened the compiler prelude in 2009 and 2010. The fixed widths, `ZZ`, `QQ` and `RR64` are siblings under `Number`, each with its own algebra, and `Number` has no catch-all operators. Why: the flattened prelude is the team's last record of the Fortress way, and its route leads to the POPL 2019 paper, which keeps the rule. He cares that specialised code runs fast, not how a specialisation is chosen. F-46 prices a return to route C.
- P-44 **`AnyIntegral`'s closure stands, and the checker reads `comprises` the 2012 way.** The closure `AnyIntegral comprises { ... }` stands, with a `NOT YET` comment in the team's wording. So do the generic scalar-extension block, the `AnyAdditiveGroup` marker and the `Array3` exclusion. A generic child of a closed trait may extend it when every type that the checker knows below it is listed. The clause's text and walk stay as they are. Row 487 records the hole that every reading but the 2008 one shares: a program's own `Integral` subtype in another component is not caught.
- P-45 **Overloads may differ in their static parameters (answer 9).** The specification drops its sentence that forbids it and states the type group's 2011 model, which the checker runs; the old sentence stays as superseded text. The checker keeps the paper's three overloading rules, checks the Return Type Rule over every instance, and requires two generic declarations in the more-specific relation to agree on their static parameters position by position, as Java's overriding rule does (row 398). Walk dispatches on declared domains, not by the order of the declarations, and its load check reads every pair of generic declarations on their declared domains by the checker's rules, with no parameter pair required to exclude, so that walk and the checker accept the same pairs (row 159). The library repairs its refused families with its own exclusions, and no model line changes. The judgement's smaller choices took the record's defaults, listed for his review in `PLAN.md`. Built: walk's load check over every pair of functions with static parameters, by climb batch 17's rung G. Not built: a functional method of a generic trait or object is still compared on its instances (F-26), the Meet Rule's search matches only some domains (row 539), two nested generic functional methods of a trait or object are refused at load where the same two functions load (row 779), and in a trait with static parameters load and fail at a call (row 780), and rows 740 and 741 wait on P-152. The one pair on which rung G's reading makes walk and the checker disagree is row 759's: walk refuses `g[\T\](a: T)` beside `g(a: Any)`, and the checker accepts it.
- P-46 **A conversion makes a call possible, and never changes which declaration runs when one already fits.** Declarations are chosen on declared domains, by applicability and then specificity (P-45). The chosen one is instantiated by answer 8's promotion (P-74), its coercions inserted statically. So beside a plain arm over `Any`, a generic arm over `T extends Number` runs at `ZZ64` for a mixed-width call. A numeral whose candidate types are incomparable reads as `ZZ32`, or as `ZZ64` or `ZZ` by its magnitude. Why: generic code is never fast, and he wants code that a JVM can specialise. His own broader rule, to convert toward a specific declaration before a generic one, is not taken. Both paths infer static arguments with coercion and the same promotion, and P-49 orders the checker's attempts. Still open: the dispatch between two generic declarations (row 537, PLAN phase 5).
- P-47 **Each integer type declares its own `MIN`, `MAX` and `MINMAX`.** It follows `QQ`, `RR64`, the compiler library and the specification's `ZZ`, so that under walk the family answers at the promoted type. Row 484's `NN32` half, a numeral beside an `NN32`, is still open.
- P-48 **A type parameter that a call's arguments do not fix takes its bound, never `Bottom`.** Its instance is the intersection of its upper bounds, constrained by the call's static return type, never the arguments' union or the value's type alone. The rule is the team's later word (POPL 2019). He ranks the team's later work above his own reading. It sets the instance, not which declaration runs (P-46). MicroGPT's types are concrete, so it is untouched. The library keeps the team's unbounded declarations. Built under walk for a reduction or comprehension that writes no static argument by climb batch 15 (`20474c144`). Still to build: a compiled dispatcher that carries the static return type (row 538, PLAN phase 5).
- P-49 **The checker tries a call without the expected type first, and with coercion only after (row 508).** It keeps the first attempt, by subtyping, when its result converts to the expected type, and only then tries coercion with the context. So a declaration that fits the arguments as they are is not passed over for one reached by coercion.
- P-50 **A `label` body takes the expected type of the whole `label` (item 48 (a)).** The specification types a `label` as the union of its body's last expression and its exits' `with` values. So the checker passes the expected type of the whole into the body and into the exits' values, as for a `typecase` clause, and the inference chapter lists both contexts. P-51 is the other half of item 48. Row 642 stays `CONTESTED` only because the ledger's tool cannot close it.
- P-51 **A call written as another call's argument is retried against each declaration's parameter type (item 48 (b), row 455).** When the checker's attempts at a call keep none, an argument that is a call with inferred static arguments is checked again, with each candidate's parameter type as its expected type. The trigger is wide: any inferred static argument, not only a result-only type parameter. Why: it makes the inference rules one rule everywhere, past the cases the team built. Its probe moves no error of the distance. Its rung promotes the expected failures `XXXInferContextDrops` and `XXXInferLoneUnionClosedTrait`, whose refusals it repairs. Built by climb batch 14 (`0856f3e6a`).
- P-52 **A range of rank 2 or 3 checks containment corner by corner (item 50, row 657).** The bounds check behind `narrowToRange` compares the other range's bounds by the ranges' point-by-point order, `PCMP`, not by the tuple order, which serves sorting. So `((0,0):(9,9)).narrowToRange((2,-1):(5,5))` raises `IndexOutOfBounds`.
- P-53 **`String`'s `left` and `right` answer `Just(c)` (item 42, row 606).** For a non-empty string they return `Just` of the first and of the last character, as their declared `Maybe[\Char\]` and every other `left` and `right` of the library do. So walk prints `Just` of the character, not the character.
- P-54 **`QQ`'s `ceiling` and `truncate` keep `ZZ` and raise at +∞, −∞ and 0/0 (item 44, row 635).** The declared integer result and the peer methods win over the specification's paragraph that returns the argument at an infinity, and that paragraph is revised. `floor`, `round` and the two brackets raise too. A rung after the switch-over makes `QQ` follow the float ruling (row 330): the methods keep the type, and the brackets, `round` and `truncate` give ℤ.
- P-55 **A size may hold arithmetic, compared by its written form once numerals are folded (item 15, 15a with (b)).** The checker accepts a sum, difference, product or power in a size. `2 3` folds to `6`, but `s0 s1` is not `s1 s0`. The class loader computes the value when it makes a class. A size name may equal a numeral, as the team's Q&A answers, so the `N[\0\]` arm of a `typecase N[\b0\]` is reachable. The library keeps the team's sizes written as products and sums. Two later array forks stand at defaults while his answers are pending: fork 3, a size known only at run time, at way 4a, where his reading of P-40 is asked; and fork 2, the bound of `Vector` and `Matrix`, at the two-trait bound (PLAN items 13 and 52).
- P-56 **The open range `(:)` keeps its wildcard type, and its five cutting methods fail (item 49, row 656).** `TrivialOpenRange` stays `OpenRange[\Any\]`. A range over `ZZ32` is not a range over `Any`, so no body can type its `truncL`, `truncR`, `every`, `imposeStride` and `atMost`. They are `fail` bodies with a message, the team's own device for such a body. Nothing in the tree calls them on `(:)`. Way (c), `(:)` over `ZZ32`, is not taken: probe P3 found it changes 64 small programs' values.
- P-57 **`LexicographicReduction.isLeftZero` takes `TotalComparison`, so the team's answers are reached (row 582).** The team's overload `isLeftZero(_:Comparison)` is declared over `TotalComparison`, so the inherited `ReductionWithZeroes.isLeftZero` no longer shadows it. `LessThan` and `GreaterThan` answer `true`, and `EqualTo` `false`. `isLeftZero(Unordered)` is refused under walk. Nothing calls `isLeftZero`. Why: it cleared the count stage's last api error (F-53).
- P-58 **Every native binding is a `builtinPrimitive` call naming a static helper (item 35).** Each binding stays the library's own form, a body that is exactly `builtinPrimitive("…")`, and its string names a static helper of `nativeHelpers/`, not an interpreter glue class. Walk loads the string through a loader beside its glue classes. The compiled path rewrites each body at the parse into a synthetic `import java` and a call before the checker, and refuses a string that names no helper. Way 2, `import java` blocks in the library, is not taken. Still to build: the natives rungs, PLAN phase 4.
- P-59 **Walk chooses coercions on the value until the switch-over.** Walk has no static types, so it chooses a coercion by the value, where the specification and the compiled path resolve it statically. This is accepted as the interpreter's limit (item 16), stated in one callout of the coercion chapter, with `XXXCoercionStaticRungC` and `XXXCoercionStaticNarrowRungC` as its record. After the switch-over walk takes the static coercions that the checker inserts. MicroGPT's static types are concrete, so both paths agree on it.
- P-60 **The specification reads a `comprises` clause at the level of values (PLAN item 26, row 491).** "Covers" is defined once, and the Meet Rule has a closed-trait case. A call whose argument sits between closed traits is typed by the intersection of its candidates' return types, with run-time uniqueness in place of static. Why: the proof addendum (`reviews/comprises-type-level-proof-addendum.md`) shows this sound for ground declarations, `G[\ZZ32\]` among them, with the coverage search local to overload checking. A generic declaration that needs a run-time instance is outside it. The specification states that boundary. The checker's condition is narrower, no static parameters in the whole family (row 543), and walk trusts the clauses' closure unchecked (row 551), both listed for his review.
- P-62 **The `covariant` keyword is future work, off the path to microGPT.** Row 404 records the hole: the checker accepts variance, and neither path carries it to run time. Its expected-failure tests are owed in a batch rung. The ledger's worklist item 12 is declaration-site variance, carried to run time on both paths. When it lands, the specification's sign-refined number types come back as covariant static parameters.
- P-146 **The checker reads `self` in a self-typed trait's method bodies as the implementing type (way 6).** In a trait `C[\X\]` whose parameter `X` extends `C[\X\]`, `self` in the trait's method bodies has the type `C[\X\] & X`; the signatures keep the plain trait type, as the POPL 2019 paper's assumption on declared types needs. A type that extends such a trait at another type is refused, Scala's conformance rule. The library's text gains no self type and no `comprises` clause, and walk is unchanged. It clears 29 sites of the distance; the thirtieth takes one `numerator` per integer type. Why: it reads the library as the team wrote it, as P-44 does, by one rule the peers share. Built by climb batch 14 (`1c32ccffd`).
- P-147 **An object defines an inherited abstract method when its bodies of that name at narrower parameter types together cover the abstract method's parameter types (item 51).** It is the team's rule of 2012, in Steele's compiled checker and Welterweight's Covered rule, with `comprises` clauses read as the checker reads them; a body at the abstract method's own types is the plain case. So the team's `Pairs` and `FileConversion` stay valid, walk agrees with the checker, and the traits chapter's sentence is revised in the S1 form (P-96). Walk's allowance of any one narrower body goes. Built by climb batch 14 (`f9fe5c874`), which first repaired rows 668 and 669.
- P-148 **The checker's speed comes right after its correctness.** A rung that changes the checker measures how the change affects the time that the checker needs. First the rung makes the change correct. Then it does a second pass that makes the checker faster. This pass must not change the checker's results: the checker accepts and refuses the same programs as before, with the same errors at the same places. The rung's skeptic checks the time and the results. This work is part of the rung, not a separate step after the landing. Built in the `fortress-repo` skill (`compiler.md`), the batch script's rung and skeptic prompts, and the batch manual.
- P-149 **An object that inherits an abstract functional method from one trait and its body from a sibling trait, and declares none of its own, is refused (Q1).** So `object O extends { A, B }`, with `pick(self)` abstract in `A` and given a body in `B`, must declare its own `pick`, as the specification's text and the type group's Welterweight calculus require and as walk already does; an abstract and a concrete declaration of one method in one trait are refused too. Why: the revival honors the designers' intent and does not change Fortress's nature for a convenience; other languages are consulted only to reconcile a conflict between earlier and later designers' choices, and here there is none. No library type uses the shape. Built by climb batch 16's rung K (`c23b85fdc`): rows 572, 727 and 734 closed.
- P-151 **Only the `where` forms the team wrote down are built.** A trait that extends another under a `where` condition is that type only where the condition holds, and its members are checked under the condition; a method's `where` condition bounds its static parameters; and the team's comment `AnyList comprises List[\E\] where [\E\]` becomes live. `SUM`'s fusion with `MAX` and `MIN` stays, the team's commented generic `distribute` measured for its two type errors; the rest of `AnyList` moves into `List`. Why: build what the team left, and add nothing it did not. Built: the method condition and the generic `distribute`, by climb batch 17's rung L (`2b1cd8e63`), and `AnyList`'s clause, by its rung A (`24db899fa`), with `AnyList`'s bodies respelled within `AnyList`, not moved into `List`; conditional extension in the compiled checker, by climb batch 18's rung X (`372b9bf6a`), and the `where` forms' checks where they apply, by its rung K (`396e4ed8d`). Still to build: the members scoped to the condition, since a member checked under it stays callable where it fails (row 773); where an object's value parameters fall under the condition (judge-review.1 of climb batch 18, its default taken: with the members); walk's half (row 774); and the code generator's half (row 701), after the switch-over (PLAN, phase 3, the `where` clauses' line).
- P-152 **Exclusion between two generic declarations is read over the whole parameter type, on both paths (the specification's existential reduction).** Two declarations whose parameter types exclude each other only together, through a shared parameter that fixes one static argument, are read as the specification reads them: the pair is valid where the declared domains meet the overloading rules. Walk and the compiled checker both change to read the whole parameter type, so that rows 740 and 741 close, and walk loads the program that it refused after climb batch 16. Why: the type group's paper of 2011 decides exclusion between parameter types with static parameters by existential reduction (`Papers/Types/exc-reduction.tick`; the team's later word, P-26), as the revised specification states (`advanced/overloading.tex`, "Declarations with Static Parameters"). Still to build: the reading on both paths, after the probe for its algorithm (PLAN phase 3, item 17).

### Numbers

- P-66 **The integer principle: Java's and the JVM's defaults stay where they make sense, and are corrected where they fail high performance or mathematical precision.** The team did so with rounding and the sign of `GCD`. A hardware behaviour that bytecode can express gets its own explicit spelling, as the specification's wrapping and saturating operators do. Where the JVM prevents a correct implementation, the project gives way for now. The peers to compare are Julia, X10, Swift and Rust.
- P-67 **`round` on an exact half goes to the even integer, on both paths.** It is the specification's rule for rationals, IEEE's default and the team's own rational body. Built.
- P-68 **`floor` and `ceiling` on the float types keep the float; ⌊x⌋, ⌈x⌉, `round` and `truncate` return the unbounded ℤ.** The library's own `truncate` and `round` are tidied to match. Still to build: a library rung after the switch-over, which first counts the interpreter tests whose output changes (row 330).
- P-69 **`LSHIFT`/`RSHIFT` are bit operators on the fixed widths; `shift` is exact on ℤ.** A count at or beyond the width gives 0 or the sign, and a negative count reverses. Shifted-out bits fall silently, as in every peer language. Compiled code shifts the machine word, never through ℤ. A count may have any integral width (row 380). Built on both paths; the compiled path gets `shift` and the any-width count at the switch-over (P-38).
- P-70 **`GCD` and `LCM` give nonnegative results, and `LCM` raises an overflow error when the multiple does not fit, on both paths.** The specification says so. Built (row 334).
- P-71 **`|0|`, `-0` and `0 DIV -1` do not overflow: an overflow guard tests for the most negative value itself, not for `a = -a`.** The compiled natives and their siblings with that guard are fixed. Built (row 333).
- P-72 **`narrow` out of range truncates to the low 32 bits, signed and unsigned, on both paths.** The team's boundary test `tests/UnsignedTest.fss` asserts it. Built (row 346).
- P-73 **Fixed-width overflow raises `IntegerOverflow` under `walk`, as the specification says and the compiled path does, `NN32` and `NN64` included.** Code that means to wrap uses the specification's operators ∔, ∸ and ⨰, fully parenthesised, since their precedence is stated only among themselves. The saturating operators wait for a step of their own. Built (row 379).
- P-74 **Mixed integer widths convert by declared coercions (answer 8, to PLAN item 8): each wider type declares a `coerce` from each narrower one, as the compiler prelude does.** An exact conversion is implicit and a lossy one explicit: `ZZ32` and integer numerals coerce into `RR64`, and `ZZ64` into `RR64` stays explicit (P-66). A generic call or a range over mixed widths infers the narrowest type that both sides coerce into. The specification's `widens` is deferred. Built; no model line changed.
- P-75 **`NN32` coerces into `RR64`, since the conversion is exact (P-74).** Not built: with that coercion, a `ZZ32` with an `NN32` is ambiguous between `RR64`'s and `ZZ64`'s operators on both paths, where P-74 gives `ZZ64`, and two team tests fail (row 575). It waits as PLAN item 37, with its candidates; not building it is the default.
- P-76 **The numeral switch, split by where the static types are: a numeral's type is `IntLiteral`, which each number type converts from, in the library now and under walk once walk has static types.** It is the compiler library's working design, taken over the specification's unfinished numeral types. A range of rank 2 or 3 is a tuple of `ZZ32` ranges, and the public range traits stay generic in their index type. Built.
- P-78 **`SUM` and `PROD` without the `Number` catch-all: one generic reduction each over the library's algebra, taking its identity from the static argument (answer 7, to PLAN item 7).** A clause form whose element type nothing at the call fixes writes its static argument, as the team's tests do; `SUM e` and `DOT` keep their text. The model's two changed lines, `MicroGptFlat.fss:28` and `:43`, are approved. `BIG MAXN`, `BIG MINN` and `BIG MINMAXN` are gone, and `MAX` and `MIN` get no identity on the integers or the floats (F-60). Built.
- P-79 **The team's demos that write no static argument for a generic reduction stay as they are, and are respelled later only if they still fail.** When a batch has a free slot, it first checks each demo again under P-48's bound rule (row 731). It then writes the static arguments that a demo still needs, with a demo stage that only reports.
- P-80 **The sign-refined number types are a superseded design: a program tests such a subset at run time.** The number chapters test a value's sign by comparison, and a float's finiteness by `check` or `check*` on `RR64`. `advanced-lib/numbers-advanced.tex` stays word for word, marked superseded in the S1 form (P-96), so that the original design stays on record. Built. Their return with covariance is P-62's.

### Arrays and the model program

- P-84 **Storage is `double[]`, unboxed, and arrays keep the team's `nat` sizes.** A high-performance language cannot box its array elements, and the sizes are central to the team's design. So both are built together: sized types, the checker taught `nat` parameters, in the library's own patterns. How `double[]` goes under a float vector is array decision A (P-85).
- P-85 **The array design's three questions are open, with no default, and return after the switch-over with array decisions A, B and D (PLAN item 13).** The three: a store per element type chosen by the factory, the size also kept as a field of the store, and a factory for a size known only at run time that returns the unsized `Array`. A is how `double[]` goes under a float vector, B where unboxed arithmetic happens, D sizes in the model's own types (P-87). Also open: why `RR64` and not `RR32`, since LLMs train at FP32 at most; the one reason given is the Python reference's float64 output. P-55 holds the forks taken before the switch-over.
- P-86 **The integration review's checks stand for the array work.** A generic `Vector` or `Matrix` body is checked against what each operation needs, with no blanket ring bound that would exclude integer arrays. An empty reduction is checked for its type and its value. A small product through `PView` and a transpose is checked, with controls. The checks: `reviews/numeric-hierarchy-integration-review.md` section 5.
- P-87 **The model's text is the notation, and the vocabulary is repaired around it.** An operator in the model never becomes a function call to satisfy an overload check. Any repair that changes a model line is shown to him as a diff before it is built. Decision D, the sized signatures of the flat program C4's vocabulary, is such a diff (`reviews/decision-d-diff.md`); nothing of it is applied before PLAN phase 5.

Gating row 331 on static-argument inference instead is parked (PLAN, "Off the path, parked").

- P-95 **Every change to the specification is recorded with its reason.** No discrepancy between the specification and the implementation stays open to confuse a reader. The original text and the reasons are kept, so that route C, the way back to the patents' forest rule (P-43), stays open. Every change takes the S1 form (P-96). `Specification-1.0-frozen/` is never touched.
- P-96 **The S1 form: a change of the specification is shown in the layered form that the team used for 1.0 and its 2009 draft.** A callout that prints in every build, not a `\note`, marks each changed passage. Appendix I's revival section gives each change its reason, its original text, the way back to route C and the decision it follows. The front matter has one paragraph on the revision, and a repository document holds the full reasoning. The unrevised copy is cited as the Working Draft of February 2011. The parts in detail: fortress-repo skill, `references/specification.md`.
- P-97 **The refused examples (S2) take the one library's shapes, under one statement of instantiation exclusion.** Each refused example stays, marked "Not allowed" as the specification marks one, beside the library's shape. The rule is stated once, in Luchangco's two-part form (P-25). The covariance example's callout adds that the type group's later design has a `covariant` modifier, which neither path implements (row 404). The calculi of Appendix A keep their rules, under a callout that they predate the rule.
- P-98 **`TotalComparison` extends `StandardMinMax[\TotalComparison\]`, so that it has `MIN` and `MAX`.** It does so in the api and in the component, and keeps its five restated members. He took it on the coordinator's recommendation and wants it explained in more detail when he has the energy, so it is on the list for his review (PLAN, "Pavol's answers, in the order they are needed").

### The suites and the gate

- P-102 **Test first, the test kept.** Every sealed-tree edit starts from a failing test added to the corpus: the worker writes the test first, verifies that it actually fails, makes the fix, proves it passes, and the test stays in the corpus from then on; the full suite stays green. The test needs no commit of its own: the test and the fix may land in one commit. How the test is written is in the `fortress-repo` skill's tests part.
- P-103 **The suite's verdict is the check.** A test passes or fails, as the team designed the suite, and a value that matters is asserted in the test with the mechanisms the suite already has (an `assert` in an interpreter test, `run_out_equals` in a compiled one). What a test prints beyond its checks does not matter. So no expected-output files are added; none of it is offered to him again.
- P-123 **Row 366's three-line fix waits for a rung of its own, and route C gets no entry in the specification's Proposed Features.** Both are batch 5's defaults, which he took: the fix is not in design B as he decided it (P-41), and Appendix I already carries route C, the alternative to the flat tower (P-96).
- P-124 **The specification's examples join the gate at zero red.** `ant testSpecData` runs them under walk as a gate step, and every example must pass. A failing example is not respelled for walk, and no list of known red examples is kept: the implementation is fixed instead. Built.
- P-125 **The suites run Fortress in parallel, pinned at four threads in `build.xml`.** Parallelism is native to Fortress, so a one-thread suite has a blind spot, and sparing a four-CPU machine is no reason for one. A test that fails or varies under parallelism is written wrong, such as a write that needs `atomic`, or it exposes a defect: either is fixed, never hidden by a pin. The pin makes every run the same, whatever the calling shell sets. Built.
- P-150 **No resident compiler is built.** One warm JVM that serves many Fortress commands, as Scala 2's `fsc` did, would save at most 1.8 % of the workers' time, so the speed work goes to the checker itself (P-148). The probes (`mie-probes/forest/`) show that the forest alone does not keep a specialisation at an inner level sound: generic code at the level below gets the specialisation's result (`IncompatibleClassChangeError`). It needs a return type rule over every level below, `comprises T` read covariantly, and dispatch ordered to match; so it is a third route that keeps the rule, the tower and specialisation, at more checker work than dropping the rule.
